title: OTTO-WASH
frame: Wash bay frame: origin at the parked car centre on grade, +Y up, X across the bay, +Z north (toward the exit). Machine at dy = 0, tools retracted.

subsystems.name: Floor rails
subsystems.function: Two steel rails, 3.25 m each side of the car, carry the machine over the parked car.
how: Anchor plates every metre hold each rail to the slab with concrete screws.
The rails stand outside the door opening.
A stop at each rail end holds a wheel if the machine runs past its travel.

subsystems.name: Travel drive
subsystems.function: Moves the whole machine back and forth over the car, 6 passes a wash.
how: A geared motor inside each trolley drives one wheel. The drives keep in step by encoder.
Side rollers keep the wheels on the rails.
Between cars, and while the arms work, the machine is stowed at the entrance end, 1.8 m behind the car.

subsystems.name: Portal frame
subsystems.function: Two legs and a beam span the bay. Retracted, everything clears a car by more than 0.48 m.
how: Bolted flanges join the legs to the trolleys and to the beam.
Galvanised steel, painted safety yellow.

subsystems.name: Spray arch
subsystems.function: Sprays the pre-soak, the wash water jets and the clear-water rinse.
how: 9 flat-fan nozzles each side and 5 across the top.
Solenoid valves switch the pre-soak, the wash water and the rinse water.
The water does the washing. No brush touches the car, its cameras or its lidar.

subsystems.name: Air knives (dryer)
subsystems.function: Blow the water off in the last 2 passes.
how: A top knife on 2 telescoping lift columns follows the car top. 2 side knives close on the flanks.
3 blowers on the beam feed the knives through flexible ducts.
A concertina duct draws out as the top knife goes down. A duct loop to each side knife swings in with it.

subsystems.name: Detail arm tracks
subsystems.function: A floor track each side of the car takes a detail arm to any place along the car.
how: 2 profile rails on a steel beam, anchored to the slab every metre.
A servo gearmotor on the carriage drives a pinion on a rack between the rails.
A cable chain beside the track brings power, network and pure water to the carriage.
The tracks stand 2.1 m from the drive line, inside the gantry rails. The gantry passes over them.

subsystems.name: Arm docks and pad care
subsystems.function: Each arm parks at the exit end, folded along its track, with its pad in a rinse cup.
how: A nozzle in the cup rinses the pad with pure water after each car. The pad turns in the cup to throw the water off.
The dock stands north of the gantry's travel, so a parked arm is never under the gantry.
A signal on each dock faces the car: red while the bay works, green when the car may go.

subsystems.name: Detail arm J1 base turn
subsystems.function: Turns the whole arm about the vertical axis.
how: A size 40 actuator in the pedestal top turns the turret.
It is the charge arm's own joint.

subsystems.name: Detail arm J2 shoulder
subsystems.function: Leans the upper arm toward or away from the car.
how: A size 50 actuator in the turret boss drives the upper arm.
A gas spring balancer carries most of the gravity load.

subsystems.name: Detail arm upper arm
subsystems.function: The 1.344 m cast link from the shoulder to the elbow.
how: A hollow aluminium casting, 7 mm wall.

subsystems.name: Detail arm J3 elbow
subsystems.function: Folds the forearm to set the reach and the height of the wrist.
how: A size 40 actuator in the upper arm boss drives the forearm.

subsystems.name: Detail arm forearm
subsystems.function: The 1.142 m cast link from the elbow to the wrist centre.
how: A hollow aluminium casting with a dog-leg, so it folds past the upper arm.

subsystems.name: Detail arm wrist (J4, J5, J6)
subsystems.function: Points the pad square onto a sensor at any angle, as a hand does.
how: The 3 wrist axes meet at one point. So the pad turns about that point and stays on the sensor.
J6 turns the pad a quarter turn each way to polish. It does not spin free, so no cable winds up.

subsystems.name: Detail arm status
subsystems.function: Light rings on the arm show its state.
how: Teal at rest, green at work, amber on the move.

subsystems.name: Polishing head
subsystems.function: A soft pad on a floating, force-sensing head polishes each camera, lidar and radar cover.
how: A 6-axis force sensor reads the push. The arm holds it at 5 N and stops at 10 N.
A floating joint lets the pad tilt 6 degrees and give 8 mm. So it lies flat on a curved cover.
The pad is microfibre over soft foam, 120 mm across. It is small enough for the edge of a roof lidar.
A camera beside the pad finds each sensor. A nozzle mists it with pure water first. No chemical is used.

specs.push: 5 N working, 10 N limit (ASSUMPTION, to be set on test)

subsystems.name: Control, supply and signals
subsystems.function: Runs the program, and tells the car when to stop and when to go.
how: A stainless control cabinet on the inner side of the west leg holds the controller and the drives.
A stop light faces the arriving car: red while the program runs, green when the car may go.
A drag chain brings power, water, chemicals and air. It lies in a covered trench in the floor, inboard of the west rail. Its fixed end is at mid travel.
A driver in the cover's slot joins its other end to the west trolley. Its bend rolls along at half the machine's speed. A conduit takes the lines up the leg to the cabinet.
Nothing stands outboard of the trolleys: the end bays' outer walls are 48 mm from them.
